title: The Effects of Educational Workshops on Self-Compassion, Perceived Sport Performance, and Team Effectiveness in Collegiate Softball Student-Athletes
abstract: Self-compassion has been explored as a valuable tool for athletes in managing failure and coping with sport-related pressures. The current study investigated whether self-compassion-focused educational workshops developed for this study can enhance collegiate softball athletes’ self-compassion, perceived sport performance, and team effectiveness. The workshops were guided by Neff’s self-compassion framework, including elements of fierce self-compassion. A one-group pretest–posttest design was used with 22 National Collegiate Athletic Association Division I softball players over a 6-week intervention. Athletes participated in weekly workshops and completed pre- and posttests of the Self-Compassion Scale, Perceived Sport Performance Scale, and Team Effectiveness Questionnaire. Paired t tests and correlation analyses were conducted to assess changes in outcomes. Results showed a significant increase in overall self-compassion, whereas perceived sport performance and team effectiveness were not significant. These findings support self-compassion as a practical tool in sport settings. Future research could expand to other teams to improve representation within the athletic population.
